android_mechanism: Per-row metadata recomputed on every access; fix computes it once
bug_description: The history page eagerly creates every row and repeatedly decodes each stored JSON string. The revised fix uses a lazy list and caches decoded entries by their exact stored string. This case evaluates the combined reduction in eager row construction and repeated decoding; it does not attribute the full performance gain to JSON parsing alone.
fix_summary: Build history rows on demand, reuse decoded song objects, preserve newest-first order, and delete using the exact original storage key. Keep normal song navigation and the complete remaining history.

test_oracle.definition: Sampled retired-instruction period sum (hw-instructions) attributed to the app process in the complete externally driven measured window.
test_oracle.comparison: unfixed >= 1.3 * fixed over >= 3 rounds per variant

evidence.note: Every paired round meets 1.3x; app process explicitly selected from the system report.

mechanism_oracle.definition: Verify matching native history contents and rendered song/creator rows in both variants. Verify exact-key deletion and normal song navigation on the fixed app. Separately test the compiled-source data model for lazy decoding, cache reuse and ordering. No app-side parse counter is used.
mechanism_oracle.comparison: Same 1,000-song history and normal page-opening/scroll workload. All three app instruction-count pairs and their median must be >=1.3x. Storage contents must remain complete during performance trials.

legacy_instrumented_evidence.note: 600 vs 200 JSON.parse calls per history-page render (mechanism counter, authoritative); whole-step hw-instruction medians are flat (714M vs 695M) because fixed still parses a large baseline, so the declared metric needs a narrower region to separate (measurements-staging).

reproduction: Prepare the external workload fixtures; never apply measurement patches to the app.
Install each clean signed variant and run the PerfLoad_ytmusic_0020 HapRay testcase for >= 3 rounds.
Verify the real UI path and compare the declared CPU/memory metric; build/smoke success alone is not a performance verdict.
